images.scene: Strict one-point perspective, perfectly symmetric composition: a narrow straight wooden fishing pier seen END-ON, starting at the bottom center edge of the frame and receding straight away from the camera over calm water, vanishing into pale morning mist at the center of the image, splitting the frame into two equal halves. The camera floats just a hand's width above the water surface, almost level with it. Moored alongside the LEFT side of the pier in the foreground: a small wooden boat with a slumped dejected fisherman sitting idle, head hanging low, holding a limp slack fishing line in the water, catching nothing. Moored alongside the RIGHT side of the pier at the same distance, same size: an identical small wooden boat completely EMPTY, with two or three fish frozen mid-leap jumping out of the water in a clean arc into that empty boat, small splashes below them. Both boats fully visible inside the frame, equal visual weight, one on each side of the pier. Quiet ironic scene, early morning sea mist, 1950s coastal village. ONLY the pier and the two boats occupy the lower half; the upper half of the image is bright, pale, hazy and empty.
